answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring a refundable, stake-backed deposit earned back only through verifiable work over time. A new identity enters through a narrow inlet: it must lock collateral, complete audited tasks, and build a reputation graph of distinct counterparties before it can vote or claim rewards. Like a river that widens only after many tributaries join, influence grows gradually with proven history, while a meadow of cheap duplicate identities stays shallow and powerless, because each copy must pay the same deposit and wait the same long season before it counts.
